title: What Radiologic Technologists Do
description: Radiologic technologists create the images doctors diagnose from: X-rays, fluoroscopy, and often CT. They position patients precisely, set exposure techniques, protect from radiation, and critique images for diagnostic quality. They work in hospitals, imaging centers, and clinics — the eyes of medicine.
standards: ALARA: as low as reasonably achievable dose
safety: Shielding and collimation on every exposure
troubleshooting: Poor image quality: check positioning, technique, motion
Uncooperative patient: adapt, immobilize gently, involve family
Equipment fault: follow downtime protocol
Contrast reaction: stop, call for help, follow protocol
citations: American Society of Radiologic Technologists guidance; American Registry of Radiologic Technologists standards; medical imaging references.
provenance: Public trade knowledge drawn from radiologic technology education, professional association guidance, and medical imaging references. Real, fact-checked records.

title: Radiation Safety: ALARA
description: Every exposure follows ALARA — as low as reasonably achievable: collimate to the anatomy, shield gonads and thyroid, use the lowest technique that diagnoses, and never repeat carelessly. The tech protects patients, self, and coworkers with time, distance, and shielding.
